messages:
sam: Heads-up — we just got a customer escalation (acct: acme-inc). After the int8 calibration swap this afternoon their p95/p99 jumped sharply on rwd-llama-13b-int8. Observed p95 0.19s -> 0.48s, p99 0.33s -> 1.7s. Happened ~2024-10-03 18:12 UTC. Routing you all in case this is related to the new quant_profile rollout.

nina: Oof. Can you paste the request ids (or a sample) and model version? Also was this on Dedicated or Hosted? :eyes:

sam: Hosted API for this tenant (prod region eu-west-1). Sample request-id: req_20241003_18_12_az9f. Model: rwd-llama-13b-v2 @ quant_profile: int8-calib-v4 (swapped from int8-calib-v3). Workload: chat completions, avg prompt ~120 tokens, seq len ~512.

kevin: Looking at metrics now — grafana link: https://grafana.redwood/team/support/d/latency?q=req_20241003_18_12 — guardrail numbers in logs:
```
metric p95_old: 0.19
metric p95_new: 0.48
metric p99_old: 0.33
metric p99_new: 1.68
inflight: steady
batch_size p50: 4 -> 9 after profile
```
Likely batching change + a KV-cache miss pattern. Not sure why batch jumped.

josh-sre: Ops-bot shows a quant-profile rollout at 2024-10-03T17:55:23Z to int8-calib-v4 (canary -> 100%). @ops-bot can you confirm rollout scope and any autoscaling events around 18:00?

ops-bot: Deployment event: quant-profile int8-calib-v4 applied to model rwd-llama-13b-v2 across region eu-west-1. Canary window: 17:55:23Z - 18:05:23Z. Autoscaler: no large scale events; minor pod churn reported 17:50-17:58.

tara: Repro steps from my end (quick):
1) curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"model":"rwd-llama-13b-v2","input":"<~120 token chat>","max_tokens":256}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions
2) set X-Region: eu-west-1 and run 50 reqs with concurrency 6 (wrk/hey)
Observed tail latency increase ~2x on p99 after swap. If I force header X-Quant-Fallback: fp16 the p99 drops back to ~0.35s.

kevin: That X-Quant-Fallback experiment is telling — fallback to fp16 reduces latency. Suggest immediate mitigation: rollback quant_profile for that model to int8-calib-v3 (or set region-level fallback gating) while we debug calibration.

nina: Agreed. Also need reproducible root cause. Two hypotheses:
- int8-calib-v4 changed dynamic range quant for attention matmul causing more memory thrash and larger batch sizes (we saw batch_size jump)
- calibration changed perf hotspots (some kernels forced to slower paths)
Share calibration logs.

sam: Pushed calibration logs from the canary job:
```
[calib] profile int8-calib-v4: quantized attention weights with per-channel scaling
[calib] fused_kernels: disabled for some fused-attn subop (fallback to reference kernel)
[calib] observed_max_seq: 512
[calib] note: kv-cache packing mode: packed-serialized -> increased io per-request
```

tara: The "fallback to reference kernel" line is a red flag. That explains slower token step. Might be a missing optimized int8 kernel for that op/target arch (A100 vs A10G differences?). Which hardware were the affected hosts on?

josh-sre: Affected hosts: pool-gpu-eu-1 (mix of A100s and T4s). Canary mapping shows most int8-canary landed on A100s but some T4 traffic hit too. int8-calib-v4 may not have compatible kernels on T4 and triggered slower path.

support_lead: Action plan proposal (short):
- Immediate: rollback int8-calib-v4 to int8-calib-v3 for eu-west-1 for model rwd-llama-13b-v2 (mitigates SLA) — @ops-bot can you schedule rollback now?
- Short-term: set per-arch gate for int8-calib-v4 so T4s remain on v3
- Mid-term: add kernel compatibility check to rollout pipeline and automated perf smoke tests (p95/p99 guardrails)
- Postmortem: triage calibration heuristics that disable fused kernels.

ops-bot: Rollback task created and executed: quant-profile set to int8-calib-v3 for rwd-llama-13b-v2 in eu-west-1 at 18:34:02Z. Canary -> 100% rollback confirmed.

kevin: After rollback metrics are trending back to baseline:
```
p95 now: 0.21s
p99 now: 0.36s
batch_size p50: reverted to 4
```
Customer confirm pending.

sam: Customer (acme-support) said latency reverted and SLA green. They requested a writeup of root cause and mitigation steps.

nina: For the postmortem I'll collect:
- calibration diff between v3->v4 (weights, per-channel vs per-tensor scaling)
- kernel availability matrix by GPU type
- canary distribution logs + batch-size distribution
- test coverage gaps
I'll attach a reproducer harness: small script that toggles header X-Quant-Fallback and runs concurrency test, plus instructions to reproduce on A100 vs T4.

tara: Quick repro script snippet:
```
for t in {1..200}; do 
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "X-Region: eu-west-1" \n    -H "X-Quant-Fallback: none" -d '{"model":"rwd-llama-13b-v2","input":"hello"}' \n    https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions &
done
wait
```
Use concurrency 6-8 and observe p99.

josh-sre: Also recommend we add a runtime check that if p99 increases > 2x after a quant-profile rollout in 10m window we automatically pause rollout and set fallback=true.

support_lead: Sounds good. I'll draft the customer message with timeline and mitigation steps and ping product for the kernel compatibility test. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

sam: Closing thread once draft is sent. Thanks everyone.
